message.content:
Since \(a\) has last digit \(5\) in base \(9\),

\[
a \equiv 5 \pmod 9.
\]

Since \(b\) has last two digits \(53\) in base \(6\),

\[
b \equiv 5\cdot 6 + 3 = 33 \pmod{36}.
\]

Reducing modulo \(9\),

\[
b \equiv 33 \equiv 6 \pmod 9.
\]

Thus

\[
a-b \equiv 5-6 \equiv -1 \equiv 8 \pmod 9.
\]

The last two digits in base \(3\) are determined by the remainder modulo \(9\). Since

\[
8 = 2\cdot 3 + 2 = 22_3,
\]

the last two digits are \(22\).

The answer is 22.
